findings.title: pop(index) leaves stale indices in map, so index() returns wrong values
findings.property: after pop(i), index(x) equals the position of x in the set's iteration order
findings.expected: 0, since the set is now OrderedSet([1])
findings.evidence: index() docstring: 'Get the index of a given entry'; add() returns the item's index. discard() renumbers map after removal, but pop() only deletes the entry and never adjusts later indices. Popping a non-last element is allowed by the documented 'Remove and return item at index'.

review.title: OrderedSet.pop(index) does not renumber map, so index() returns stale positions after popping a non-last element
review.reason: The source shows pop() does `del self.items[index]; del self.map[elem]` and never decrements the map values for the items after the removed one. discard() does that renumbering (`if v >= i: self.map[k] = v - 1`), so the two removal paths leave the set in different states. The invariant `map[items[i]] == i` is broken, so index(), get_loc() and later add() calls give wrong results. For example, after pop(0) on OrderedSet([0, 1]), index(1) returns 1 while the set is [1]. The repro uses documented API (`pop(index)` is documented to remove the item at index) and failed every time. A maintainer would accept a fix that renumbers the map after popping a non-last index, as discard() does.

findings.reproSource:
from ordered_set import OrderedSet


def test_repro_pop_stale_index():
    s = OrderedSet([0, 1])
    assert s.pop(0) == 0
    assert list(s) == [1]
    assert s.index(1) == 0

review.title: symmetric_difference_update leaves duplicate items when `other` contains repeated elements
review.reason: `other` is typed `SetLike[T]`, which allows lists, and `symmetric_difference` already handles repeats correctly (`OrderedSet().symmetric_difference([0, 0])` gives `[0]`). In `symmetric_difference_update`, `items_to_add = [item for item in other if item not in self]` is not de-duplicated, so `_update_items` sets `items` to `[0, 0]` while `map` has one key. That breaks the OrderedSet uniqueness invariant, and builtin `set.symmetric_difference_update` also de-duplicates. A fix is small, for example by iterating over `dict.fromkeys(other)`, and a maintainer would likely accept it.

from ordered_set import OrderedSet


def test_repro_symdiff_update_dups():
    s = OrderedSet()
    s.symmetric_difference_update([0, 0])
    assert list(s) == [0]
    assert list(OrderedSet().symmetric_difference([0, 0])) == [0]
